name: Seerr
description: Search/execute over the Seerr REST API, catalog from the seerr-api.yml OpenAPI spec.

authMethod.help: Local user (recommended): the server signs in with its own Seerr account via /auth/local. API key: Seerr's single global key.

apiKey.help: Settings → General → API Key. Acts as the original admin (user 1) unless 'Act as user ID' is set. Stops working if the key is regenerated in Seerr.

actAsUserId.help: Optional. Sends X-API-User so calls run with that user's permissions. Anyone holding the key can still act as any user.

specBaseUrl.help: Leave empty to fetch seerr-api.yml from GitHub. Set a mirror whose layout is <url>/<git ref>/seerr-api.yml if this server can't reach GitHub.

connection.help:
**Recommended: a dedicated local Seerr user.** Seerr has no service accounts or per-user API keys, so the server signs in as its own local user. This works alongside Plex sign-in.

1. In Seerr, check that **Settings → Users → Enable Local Sign-In** is on (the default).
2. **Users → Create Local User**: enter an email (it doesn't have to be a real mailbox) and set the password yourself. Leaving it blank only works if Seerr email notifications are configured.
3. Edit the new user's **permissions**. New users get the default permissions; grant only what this server needs (e.g. Request + Manage Requests; Admin only if it should manage settings and users).
4. Enter that email and password here. The server re-signs in when its Seerr session expires.

Plex-imported users can't be used: they have no local password.
